title: Deployments, Rolling Updates and Deployment Strategies

header.html: Understand Deployments and how to perform rolling updates; Use Kubernetes primitives to implement common deployment strategies (e.g. blue/green or canary)

toc.title: Batch changes with pause and resume
Blue/green and canary with Services and labels

html:
1How a Deployment works

A Deployment describes the Pods you want (the Pod template) and how many. It creates a ReplicaSet for each version of the template. A ReplicaSet keeps the right number of Pods running. When you change the template (image, command, environment, labels), the Deployment makes a new ReplicaSet and moves the Pods over to it, a few at a time. Changing only replicas does not create a new revision.

Command What it does
k create deployment api --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=3 create
k set image deployment api nginx=nginx:stable-alpine change an image (container=image) and start a rollout
k scale deployment api --replicas=5 change the number of Pods (no rollout)
k rollout status deployment api wait for the rollout to finish
k rollout history deployment api list revisions (--revision=2 shows one)
k rollout undo deployment api go back to the previous revision (--to-revision=N for another)
k rollout restart deployment api restart all Pods one by one with the same template
k rollout pause deployment api / resume batch several changes into one rollout

The container name is in k get deploy api -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[*].name}'. For kubectl create deployment --image=nginx:alpine it is nginx.

2Rolling update settings

The default strategy is RollingUpdate. Two numbers (each a number or a percentage) control how fast it goes:

Field Meaning Default
maxSurge how many Pods above replicas may exist during the update 25% (rounded up)
maxUnavailable how many Pods may be missing during the update 25% (rounded down)

maxSurge: 2, maxUnavailable: 0 means: start two new Pods first, and only remove an old Pod when a new one is Ready: no capacity loss, more temporary Pods. Both cannot be 0.

k patch deployment api -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"rollingUpdate":{"maxSurge":2,"maxUnavailable":0}}}}'

Other fields you meet in tasks:

Field Meaning Default
minReadySeconds a new Pod must stay Ready this long before it counts as available 0
progressDeadlineSeconds after this many seconds without progress the rollout is marked failed (it is not rolled back) 600
revisionHistoryLimit how many old ReplicaSets are kept for rollout undo 10
strategy.type: Recreate stop all old Pods, then start the new ones (downtime; no two versions at once)

To change from RollingUpdate to Recreate you must also remove the rollingUpdate block: {"strategy":{"type":"Recreate","rollingUpdate":null}}.

A stuck rollout

If the new Pods never become Ready (a bad image tag, a failing readiness probe), the rolling update stops: the old Pods keep serving (that is the point), the new ones show ErrImagePull or 0/1 Ready, and rollout status waits. Read k describe pod and k rollout history, then repair or roll back with k rollout undo deployment <name>.

Revisions and change cause

Each template change makes a revision. rollout history shows CHANGE-CAUSE only if the annotation kubernetes.io/change-cause is set on the Deployment: k annotate deployment api kubernetes.io/change-cause="upgrade to stable". (The old --record flag is deprecated.)

3Batch changes with pause and resume

Every template change starts a new rollout. When a task needs several changes, pause first, so there is one rollout:

k rollout pause deployment web
k set image deployment web nginx=nginx:stable-alpine
k set resources deployment web -c nginx --limits=memory=128Mi
k rollout resume deployment web

4Blue/green and canary with Services and labels

Kubernetes has no special "blue/green" or "canary" object. You build them from Deployments, labels and a Service, because a Service sends traffic to every Ready Pod whose labels match its selector.

Strategy How
Blue/green Run the old (blue) and the new (green) version side by side, each with its own Deployment and a version label. The Service selects version: blue. When green is Ready, change the Service selector to green: all traffic moves at once. Switching back is another one-line change.
Canary Keep the stable Deployment and add a small second Deployment (the canary) whose Pods carry the same label the Service selects plus a different track label. The Service spreads requests over all Pods, so the share of canary traffic is roughly canary replicas / total replicas: 1 of 5 is about 20%. To go on, scale the canary up and the stable down; to abort, delete the canary. 
# blue/green switch
k patch service shop -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop","version":"green"}}}'
# canary: stable has 4 replicas, canary 1; both have the label app=shop, the Service selects only app=shop
k get pods -l app=shop --show-labels

The stable and canary Deployments need different selector.matchLabels (add the track label), otherwise they would fight over each other's Pods.

Rolling update Blue/green Canary
Extra capacity small (maxSurge) a full second copy a few Pods
Switch gradual instant gradual, you decide
Rollback rollout undo change the selector back delete the canary
Both versions serve at once yes, briefly no yes, on purpose
Exam tip

. For "switch traffic to green", change the Service selector and verify with k get endpoints <svc> or a request from a Pod. Do not delete the blue Deployment unless the task says so.

Exam tip

. A manifest rejected with "selector does not match template labels" means spec.selector.matchLabels must be a subset of spec.template.metadata.labels. A Deployment's selector cannot be changed after creation.

5Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m05 -->

Lab 5.1: rollback stuck update

Domain: Deployment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-01-rollback-stuck-update)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace roll, the Deployment web (3 replicas) was updated to an image tag that does not exist, and the update is stuck. Roll the Deployment back to the previous working revision and make sure all 3 replicas are Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n roll rollout history deployment web
kubectl -n roll rollout undo deployment web
kubectl -n roll rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Lab 5.2: rolling update strategy

Domain: Deployment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-02-rolling-update-strategy)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace strat, the Deployment api runs 4 replicas of nginx:alpine. Change its rolling update settings to maxSurge: 2 and maxUnavailable: 0, then update the image to nginx:stable-alpine and wait for the rollout to finish.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n strat patch deployment api -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"rollingUpdate":{"maxSurge":2,"maxUnavailable":0}}}}'
kubectl -n strat set image deployment api nginx=nginx:stable-alpine
kubectl -n strat rollout status deployment api --timeout=120s

Lab 5.3: pause batch changes

Domain: Deployment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-03-pause-batch-changes)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace roll, make two changes to the Deployment web in a single rollout: update its image to nginx:stable-alpine and set a memory limit of 128Mi on its container. Use kubectl rollout pause and resume so that kubectl rollout history deployment web lists exactly two revisions (1 and 2) afterwards, and wait until all replicas are Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n roll rollout pause deployment web
kubectl -n roll set image deployment web nginx=nginx:stable-alpine
kubectl -n roll set resources deployment web -c nginx --limits=memory=128Mi
kubectl -n roll rollout resume deployment web
kubectl -n roll rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s
kubectl -n roll rollout history deployment web

Lab 5.4: blue green switch

Domain: Deployment | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-04-blue-green-switch)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace bg, a blue version (Deployment app-blue) and a green version (Deployment app-green) of an application are both running. The Service shop currently sends all traffic to the blue version. Switch the live traffic to the green version by changing the Service, and leave both Deployments running (so that you can switch back).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n bg get svc shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
kubectl -n bg patch service shop -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop","version":"green"}}}'
kubectl -n bg get endpoints shop

Lab 5.5: canary by replicas

Domain: Deployment | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-05-canary-by-replicas)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace canary, the Deployment shop-stable (4 replicas, labels app=shop) serves version v1 through the Service shop. Add a canary: create a Deployment shop-canary with 1 replica, whose Pods carry the labels app=shop and track=canary and run the image nginx:alpine with the container command sh -c "echo v2 > /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html; exec nginx -g 'daemon off;'". Do not change the Service or the stable Deployment. About one request in five must then be answered by v2.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n canary apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: shop-canary}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: shop, track: canary}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: shop, track: canary}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:alpine
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo v2 > /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html; exec nginx -g 'daemon off;'"]
Y
kubectl -n canary rollout status deployment shop-canary --timeout=120s
kubectl -n canary get pods -l app=shop --show-labels

Lab 5.6: recreate strategy

Domain: Deployment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-06-recreate-strategy)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace strat, the Deployment batchapp (3 replicas of nginx:alpine) must never run two versions at once. Change its strategy to Recreate, keep only 2 old ReplicaSets (revisionHistoryLimit: 2), then update the image to nginx:stable-alpine and wait for the rollout to finish.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n strat patch deployment batchapp -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"type":"Recreate","rollingUpdate":null},"revisionHistoryLimit":2}}'
kubectl -n strat set image deployment batchapp nginx=nginx:stable-alpine
kubectl -n strat rollout status deployment batchapp --timeout=120s

Lab 5.7: fix selector mismatch

Domain: Deployment | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m05-07-fix-selector-mismatch)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The manifest ~/work/deploy.yaml defines the Deployment web (2 replicas of nginx:alpine, Pod label app: webapp) in the namespace roll, but kubectl apply -f rejects it. Fix the manifest without changing the Pod template label, create the Deployment, and wait until both replicas are Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl apply -f ~/work/deploy.yaml
sed -i 's/^      app: web$/      app: webapp/' ~/work/deploy.yaml
kubectl apply -f ~/work/deploy.yaml
kubectl -n roll rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

<!-- /LABS -->

6Recall questions

R1Which command undoes the last rollout?

Show the answer

kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>.

R2What do maxSurge and maxUnavailable control?

Show the answer

The extra Pods allowed and the Pods allowed to be missing during a rolling update.

R3What happens to a rolling update whose new Pods never become Ready?

Show the answer

It stops; the old Pods keep serving, and you repair it or roll back with rollout undo.

R4How do you apply several template changes in one rollout?

Show the answer

rollout pause, make the changes, then rollout resume.

R5How do you implement blue/green with Kubernetes objects?

Show the answer

Two Deployments with a version label and one Service; switch by changing the Service selector.

R6How is the traffic share of a canary set?

Show the answer

By the number of canary Pods compared with all Pods that match the Service selector.

R7What does strategy.type: Recreate do?

Show the answer

It stops all old Pods before it starts the new ones.

R8Does kubectl scale create a new revision?

Show the answer

No; only a change to the Pod template does.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Update set image, rollout status/history/undo, maxSurge/maxUnavailable
Stuck rollout old Pods stay; new Pods ErrImagePull or not Ready; fix with rollout undo
Batch rollout pause ... resume
Settings minReadySeconds, progressDeadlineSeconds (600), revisionHistoryLimit (10)
Recreate type: Recreate and rollingUpdate: null
Blue/green two Deployments, Service selector switch
Canary same Service label, different track; share = canary Pods / all Pods
Immutable a Deployment's selector cannot change
